actual_scope: At p=19, beta0=-1/2, bandwidth 2, and t_i=i, is the tail of p^{-20} sum_{j<J} Q^j H* strictly below p^{10} exp(-p^2) for J=ceil(p^{42})?
scope_change_reason: The eigenvalues of this section lie strictly inside (0, 1-p^{-40}). The named comparison is the geometric tail at r=1-p^{-40}; that coarser majorant is too large, and the checked bound is the identity Q^J H^{-1}.
bottleneck_link: FINE-PRIME.md bounds that polynomial inverse by p^{10} exp(-p^2). The HALO error identity is P - H^{-1} = -Q^J H^{-1}. On this section (1-p^{-40})^J < exp(-p^2) and ||H^{-1}||_2 < 319/100, so the error is strictly below (319/100) exp(-p^2).
stop_rule: Stop once the tail is compared with p^{10} exp(-p^2). Do not form Q and do not compare the tail with 2^{-Cp}.
evidence: research/gaussian-origin-q-tail proves exp(p^{-40}) < (1-p^{-40})^{-1}, hence (1-19^{-40})^{19^{42}} < exp(-361). The tail 2-norm is strictly below (319/100) exp(-361) and hence below 19^{10} exp(-361). The coarser majorant 19^{20}(1226/625) r^J is strictly above that threshold.
